title: Issue tokens that nobody can mistake for cards or trace back to them

blocks.text: The gateway's token vault went live last week, and the incident list is already long:

items: the checkout's card-number check refuses nine tokens in ten;
a token reached a card issuer's authorization system, as if it were a card;
a customer who shops at a café and at a garage has the same token at both;
on Tuesday a customer paid with his saved card, and another customer's card was charged;
the assessor found card numbers in clear among the things the vault keeps.

blocks.text: `tokenize` and `detokenize` in `src/main/java/com/example/practice/TokenVault.java` already work. Finish the three methods marked `TODO`: `key`, `issue` and `newToken`. The comment on each says what it is for. Tokens are 16 digits, like the cards they replace. Draw each digit with `random.nextInt(10)`, one at a time and in order, because the tests script those digits. About twelve lines in total.
`detokenize` still hands a card number to anyone who asks. The next practice deals with that.

cases.says: a card gets a 16-digit token, the same requestor gets the same token again, another card gets another, and each token leads back to its card
every token ends with the Luhn check digit of its first fifteen digits, so checks built for card numbers accept it
every token starts with the range reserved for tokens, so it can never be a real card number
the same card presented by two requestors gets two different tokens
apart from the range and the check digit, a token's digits are drawn at random; none are copied from the card
a new draw that equals an issued token is drawn again, so the issued token keeps leading to its own card
nothing the vault keeps holds a clear card number: it files tokens under the keyed lookup value

origin.section: 14.4. A Token Belongs to the Requestor It Was Issued To

concepts: A token is issued per requestor and found through the keyed lookup value, never the card number, so a token leaked from one merchant is useless at another.

A token's digits are random, not derived from the card; it has sixteen digits and a correct check digit so card-number systems accept it, and a reserved BIN so it can never be a real card; a draw already taken is drawn again.
